claims.text: Traefik chart 41.6 runs one replica by default (deployment.replicas: 1); apps/traefik.yaml sets no replicas, so staging runs one Traefik Pod.
claims.source_hint: helm show values traefik --repo https://traefik.github.io/charts --version 41.6.1 (deployment.replicas); don-hang stage-3 apps/traefik.yaml

claims.text: In MetalLB layer 2 mode, when the announcing node stops, a speaker on another node announces the address from its own node; calls sent in the meantime to the stopped node fail.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 mode > Load-balancing behavior / Limitations (failover); capture traefik-ha.txt 'announced by donhang-worker2'

claims.text: A topology spread constraint is set in the Pod spec (topologySpreadConstraints) and spreads matching Pods over the values of the topologyKey node label; with DoNotSchedule, maxSkew bounds the difference between a value's count of matching Pods and the lowest such count.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Scheduling > Pod Topology Spread Constraints > Spread constraint definition (maxSkew)

claims.text: With whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule the scheduler does not place a Pod where it would break maxSkew; a Pod with no allowed node stays Pending.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Topology Spread Constraints > whenUnsatisfiable (DoNotSchedule, the default)

claims.text: kubernetes.io/hostname is a well-known label the kubelet sets on every node to the node's hostname (in kind, the node's name), so topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname makes each node its own domain.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > Well-Known Labels, Annotations and Taints > kubernetes.io/hostname

claims.text: nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor (GA since Kubernetes 1.33) leaves out of the spread calculation nodes whose taints the Pod does not tolerate; the control-plane node carries a taint so ordinary Pods are not placed on it, so it does not count.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Topology Spread Constraints > nodeTaintsPolicy; feature gate NodeInclusionPolicyInPodTopologySpread (stable 1.33); Well-Known Taints node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane

claims.text: labelSelector in a spread constraint selects which Pods are counted; Traefik chart 41.6 labels its Pods app.kubernetes.io/name: traefik.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Topology Spread Constraints > labelSelector; helm template traefik --version 41.6.1 (Deployment Pod labels)

claims.text: Traefik chart 41.6 values deployment.replicas, topologySpreadConstraints, resources, ingressClass.name/isDefaultClass and service.spec.type are copied into its Deployment's Pod template, IngressClass and Service.
claims.source_hint: helm show values traefik --version 41.6.1 and the chart's templates (_podtemplate.tpl, ingressclass.yaml, service.yaml)

claims.text: The traefik-ha LoadBalancer Service sets no externalTrafficPolicy, so it keeps the default Cluster, and kube-proxy on the announcing node sends each connection to a ready Traefik Pod on that node or another.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies; helm template traefik --version 41.6.1 with traefik-ha-values.yaml (Service has no externalTrafficPolicy)

claims.text: When a node's kubelet stops reporting, after a grace period the control plane (node controller) sets the node's Ready condition to Unknown and marks its Pods not ready, removing them from ready Service endpoints; until then they stay listed as ready.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes > Node controller / Node status conditions (Unknown); capture traefik-ha.txt READY Unknown

claims.text: In the lab, calls keep failing after MetalLB has moved the address, because some connections still go to the paused node's Traefik and echo-ip Pods until they are marked not ready (failover ~8 s, last failure ~52 s, DECISIONS 2026-10-06).
claims.source_hint: don-hang stage-3 scripts/k8s/traefik-ha.sh comment lines 35-38; DECISIONS.md §3 2026-10-06 /repo-stage 3 F2 ('traefik-ha lỗi cuối ~52 s sau pause')

claims.text: Without a spread constraint of its own, the scheduler only prefers to spread a Deployment's Pods over nodes (default constraints use ScheduleAnyway) and never moves Pods already running, so two replicas can land on one node.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Topology Spread Constraints > Cluster-level default constraints / Built-in default constraints; Known limitations (no rebalancing)

claims.text: If no Traefik Pod is ready on a running node, MetalLB moving the address does not help: calls keep failing until one is.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (no ready endpoints → connection fails); metallb.io: Concepts (MetalLB only announces the address)

claims.text: When each replica must carry the whole load while another is down, size each replica's resource requests for the whole load, not a share of it.
High availability for an entry point means it recovers by itself after a short gap in which some requests fail, not that no request fails.
The kubelet reserves at least a container's request for it; a container may use more than its request only when the node has that resource available.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Configuration > Resource Management for Pods and Containers (intro; Requests and limits)

claims.text: Each node of a kind cluster is a Docker container, and docker pause freezes all processes in a container, so a paused kind node stops answering like a stopped machine.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start / Design (nodes are Docker containers); Docker CLI reference: docker container pause
